prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: concussion. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1247; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss came in from the claimant, who reported a side impact at an intersection and said the other vehicle entered on a red light. The claimant was not represented by counsel and confirmed they were the driver named on the policy.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report, which confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the collision. Scene photos supplied by the claimant show damage to the driver side door and rear quarter panel, though no independent witnesses have come forward.

Entry 3: Spoke with the claimant about the injury, which was reported as a concussion. The symptoms described are plausible for a collision of this type, and the claimant has no known prior injury to the head or neck area.

Entry 4: Reviewed the vehicle's service records and prior claim history, and nothing suggests the damage predates the start of coverage. No earlier damage to the vehicle is on file.

Entry 5: Treatment followed a typical course, with follow-up visits tapering as the claimant's symptoms improved. Still unclear from the repair estimate and photos whether all of the listed damage stems from this impact, so a secondary inspection has been requested.

Entry 6: The claimant has given the same account of the collision in every conversation so far, with no changes to the sequence of events. File remains open pending the inspection results and final medical documentation.
